Surface texture of affected seeds — several seeds show a dull, matte, slightly rough or chalky surface texture rather than a smooth, slightly glossy coat. Some show what appears to be a faint whitish dusty coating over portions of the seed surface.

vision_features.summary: Two opened, dry, mature seed pods are displayed with their seeds exposed and scattered on a dark background. The seeds show striking variability in color and surface condition, ranging from normal pale yellow/cream to heavily discolored dark brown, reddish-brown, and grayish-white tones. Several seeds are visibly shrunken, wrinkled, or misshapen compared to the few plump, normal-appearing seeds in the group. The inner walls of the pods also show irregular dark brown staining. The most striking visual feature is the severe and varied discoloration and shriveling affecting a large proportion of the seeds within what appear to be otherwise matured pods.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. ────────────────────────────────────────

DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. chalky white mold on cracked/shriveled seeds
Diaporthe: Diaporthe produces sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins on lower stems, and most distinctively, linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems; interior of lower stems may show irregular thin black 'zone' lines.
Phomopsis: Phomopsis is characterized by cracked, shriveled seeds covered with chalky white mold, and infected seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.
Decision rule  : IF black specks arranged in linear rows are visible on mature stems, suspect Diaporthe (pod and stem blight); IF seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold or seedlings show pinpoint reddish-brown lesions on cotyledons, suspect Phomopsis seed/seedling infection.
